definitions.explanation: A polite, euphemistic word for having a bowel movement, especially the regularity of one. Standard in medical settings, ads for digestive products, and conversation with the elderly or children.

examples.japanese: ⟦{毎朝|まいあさ}→毎朝：00966_maiasa⟧お{通|つう}じ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あって→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦{調子|ちょうし}→調子：03491_choushi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: I have a bowel movement every morning, so I'm doing well.

examples.japanese: ⟦ヨーグルト→ヨーグルト：11133_yooguruto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧⟦{食|た}べたら→食べる：00396_taberu⟧、お{通|つう}じ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: After eating yogurt every day, my bowel movements became more regular.

notes:
Polite お + ⟦{通|つう}じ→通じる：02289_tsuujiru⟧ (passing through). The polite お- is essentially fixed — saying just ⟦{通|つう}じ→通じる：02289_tsuujiru⟧ for this meaning sounds unnatural. Standard in clinical questions, ads, and any context where directness would feel crude.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{通|つう}じ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧: to have a bowel movement
- お{通|つう}じ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧: to be constipated (without a bowel movement)
- お{通|つう}じ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧よい: to be regular
- お{通|つう}じ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{整|ととの}える→整える：04259_totonoeru⟧: to regulate bowel movements

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{便|べん}→便：26147_ben⟧: stool — clinical/direct
- {便通|べんつう}: bowel movement — medical register, without the polite お-
- ⟦{便秘|べんぴ}→便秘：05383_benpi⟧: constipation
